name: details-target-reconciliation
body:
Reconciliation (apg-details-target): align the durable spec's `details` edge-kind definition with the shipped behaviour.

SOURCE STATEMENT (work brief; decided with the human — Option A, not reopened). The `details` edge kind has a write/load asymmetry. WRITE: the `details` arm of `rust.apg.layers.validate.validate_edge` (`src/layers/validate.rs`) requires only a `note` SOURCE and exempts the target from parsing, so it accepts a `Note`→`Note` `details` edge. LOAD: the projection's `Details` target list (`rust.apg.load.tables.spec_rel_pairs`, `src/load/tables.rs`) deliberately omits `Note`, so the accepted pair is dropped with no error and is invisible to `apg_query`. Result: data loss with no diagnostic. DECISION [with user]: tighten the WRITE surface to refuse `Note`→`Note` `details`; the projection's deliberate exclusion is canonical and stays unchanged (no schema/DB change). `Reviews` (`Feedback`→`Note`) is a non-goal and is untouched.

SPEC AUTHORING (this change-set). Added `requirements.stakeholder.spec-author`, the requirement `requirements.requirement.details-target-set-consistency` (feature `durable-spec-integrity`), the domain entity `domain.entity.details-edge`, its law `domain.constraint.details-canonical-target-set`, and the solution component `solution.component.details-target-validation`. The component is `implemented-by` `rust.apg.layers.validate.validate_edge` ONLY. `rust.apg.load.tables.spec_rel_pairs` (and the projection / schema generally) is deliberately NOT an `implemented-by` target: it is unchanged, and naming it would force a plan task on untouched code — so the projection's deliberate exclusion is expressed through the domain entity and its law, not as a solution target. [autonomous]

STALE-PROSE RECONCILIATION. Two durable notes asserted the old asymmetry as present-tense fact; both bodies were amended in place (edge-preserving `apg node update`), each attached here through the non-note hub it serves (a `details` edge cannot point at a `Note`):
(1) `requirements.note.cache-key-classification-folding` — its "SIBLING, NOT DUPLICATED" paragraph said a `Note`→`Note` `details` edge "was written to the node files and then silently dropped from the graph ... even though the write-time validator accepts the target". Amended: the write surface now REFUSES the pair (`rust.apg.layers.validate.validate_edge`), matching the projection's deliberate exclusion. Hub: `requirements.requirement.fast-project-start`.
(2) `requirements.note.graph-first-test-fqn-repoint` — its Attachment paragraph said "because `Details` admits no Note->Note target" while the write-time validator accepted the target. Amended to name the write refusal and the projection exclusion as one canonical rule. Hub: `requirements.requirement.graph-first-navigation`.
A query for the old asymmetry (`body CONTAINS 'silently dropped' OR body CONTAINS 'write-time validator accepts'`) now returns no note. No other note asserted it: `requirements.note.graph-first-test-pending` and `requirements.note.blacklist-not-in-cache-key` were checked, as was every note whose body carries both "Note" and "Details" (only the two above matched). [autonomous]

TEST TREATMENT. The flipped `unit`-tier test (`src/layers/tests.rs`, currently `rust.apg.layers.tests.unit.details_accepts_any_target_and_enforces_note_source`, lines 529-568) is NOT an `implemented-by` target: the flip makes its name describe the opposite behaviour, so it is expected to be renamed and a pinned old FQN would drift. It stays in the `unit` submodule per `global.constraint.test-tier-boundaries`; the plan carries it as a `modifies`/`renames` task. Sibling tests that stay green untouched: `rust.apg.layers.tests.unit.every_edge_kind_accepts_a_valid_shape` (its `details` shapes target non-`Note` authored nodes — still accepted), `rust.apg.layers.tests.unit.details_to_code_fqn_is_not_flagged` (code targets stay exempt), `rust.apg.load.tests.unit.reviews_pairs_admit_note_but_details_still_excludes_it` (projection unchanged), and `rust.artifacts_e2e.e2e.illegal_details_pair_is_projected_away_not_a_binder_error`.

SCOPE. The tightening is on the durable `apg edge add` surface (`validate_edge`) only. The transient plan-JSONL path that produced the e2e's `Note`→`Note` pair writes records directly and never calls `validate_edge`; its project-away behaviour is unchanged and that e2e stays green as-is. [judgment call — flagged for review]
